name: Confluence
verdict: A private Atlassian OAuth app takes about 5 minutes and no review. Sharing it with customers is self-serve but needs vendor details, policy links and a personal data declaration. For an agent that stores or caches Confluence data, that declaration brings reporting obligations.

creation.label: Easy
creation.note: About 5 minutes in our test, across three console pages.

approval.label: Self-serve
approval.note: No review to share an OAuth app. Marketplace listing is separate.

handsOn.note: Minutes for the app; longer if you need a privacy policy and a personal data reporting setup.

waiting.note: Sharing takes effect when you save it.

ownApp.headline: Check Composio first.
ownApp.note: We could not confirm a Composio-managed Atlassian app.

oneWayDoors.title: Access type is set at creation.
oneWayDoors.detail: Resource-level limits access to the one site the user picks (acme.atlassian.net). Account-level reaches every site in the customer's account. Neither is preselected.
oneWayDoors.doThis: Pick Resource-level unless your agent truly needs every site.

oneWayDoors.title: The personal data answer is almost always Yes for agents.
oneWayDoors.detail: You must say Yes if you store personal data tied to Atlassian account IDs in your systems, or cache any data for longer than 24 hours.
oneWayDoors.doThis: Decide your caching and memory design before you share, and plan for the Personal data reporting API.

oneWayDoors.title: Stopping sharing affects existing users.
oneWayDoors.detail: The console warns that switching back to Not sharing may affect existing app users.
oneWayDoors.doThis: Share only when ready to support customers.

items.name: Forge app

notes.title: Classic vs granular scopes
notes.text: Atlassian has two scope systems. After adding only classic scopes, the console warned that the Confluence API had no granular scopes. Newer endpoints need granular scopes; mixing them up is a common cause of 401 errors.

scopes.intro: Scopes are added per API (Confluence, Jira, User identity, Personal data reporting and more). Atlassian recommends no more than 50 scopes in total.

minimalSets.label: "Answer from our wiki" agent
minimalSets.note: Check each endpoint's docs for whether it wants granular scopes.

changingLater: Edit scopes on the Permissions page; users must reauthorize to grant new ones.

toCreate: An Atlassian account; agreement to Atlassian's developer terms
The Composio callback URL (up to 30 callback URLs allowed)
forApproval: Vendor name, privacy policy URL, terms of service URL, support contact
A personal data decision, and Personal data reporting API handling if Yes

steps.title: Sign in to developer.atlassian.com
steps.detail: Console, My apps. A new Developer Space selector may appear.

steps.title: Create, OAuth 2.0 integration
steps.detail: Name the app and choose Resource-level access.

steps.title: Agree to developer terms and create
steps.detail: The page notes rotating refresh tokens are mandatory for new apps.

steps.title: Add the Confluence API and scopes
steps.detail: Permissions, Confluence API, Configure, Edit scopes. Choose classic or granular per the endpoints you call.

steps.title: Add OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and the callback
steps.detail: Authorization page, then paste the Composio callback. The page then generates an authorization URL.

steps.title: Fill distribution details and share
steps.detail: Vendor name, policy links, support contact, personal data answer, then switch to Sharing.

stepsNote: In our test: about 5 minutes to a private app with scopes and callback. Sharing was not switched on (needs real policy URLs).

approval.whenNeeded: No review to share an OAuth 2.0 app. Atlassian Marketplace listing is a separate path.
approval.renewal: If you declared personal data: ongoing reporting through the Personal data reporting API.

ladder.limit: Customers cannot authorize until Sharing is on.

ladder.works: Shared app, any site via your URL.
ladder.limit: Resource-level apps see only the site the user picked.
Rate limit tier shown on the app; reporting duties if you store personal data.

rows.refresh: Rotating, mandatory for new apps; reuse is detected

rules.title: Personal data declaration.
rules.text: Yes if you store personal data with account IDs or cache data longer than 24 hours.

rules.title: Personal data reporting.
rules.text: Apps that store personal data report the accounts they hold, so deleted or changed users can be handled.

impact.title: Design impact
impact.text: Agent memory or a vector index of Confluence pages counts as storing data. Decide this before you share.

credentialHandoff.summary: Console-only creation as far as we found. An agent can do every step after sign-in; the secret can be copied into Composio.

blockers.fix: Add the granular scopes the endpoint documents
Provide vendor details and switch to Sharing
Store the newest refresh token every time
Expected; users connect each site, or use Account-level
